surface_fix.exact_change: 1) install-nightly-task.ps1: the daily trigger gets a Repetition (New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -Daily -At 21:30 then $trigger.Repetition = (New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -Once -At 21:30 -RepetitionInterval (New-TimeSpan -Hours 1) -RepetitionDuration (New-TimeSpan -Hours 8)).Repetition, StopAtDurationEnd) so occurrences exist at 21:30, 22:30 ... 05:30; each is independent, so the first one after a sign-in fires, and the LAST one (05:30) still has a 60-minute window against the 06:30 hard stop, above MinMinutes 12. Nothing can fire in daylight: the duration ends 05:30 and the chain's own two clocks (HardStop 06:30, MaxMinutes 150) are untouched. Comment the constant with what else was considered (a logon trigger was rejected because a 07:31 sign-in would hold the card through the 08:00 sweep; S4U was rejected because the chain ends in git push through the signed-in user's credential store). 2) nightly.ps1: a pure Test-AlreadyRanThisWindow -Now -WindowStart -Status that returns the skip reason when the status file's `started` is at or after the current night's 21:30 AND its stages carry a resolve stage at OK or PARTIAL; when it returns a reason the chain records 'window' 'SKIPPED' 'already ran this night at <started>' and exits 0 WITHOUT rewriting graph-nightly-status.json (the stamp must keep the real run's figures) and without starting the transcript. A WINDOW-refused or crashed earlier occurrence (no resolve stage) does NOT count as ran, so the next repetition retries. 3) nightly.ps1: move Start-RunLog below the -StopOnly and -WhatIfOnly branches so only the chain writes graph-nightly-<date>.log; if a record of -StopOnly is wanted, name it 'graph-nightly-stoponly' and route it through Done so it carries the rc stamp. 4) Re-register with `powershell -File graph/pipeline/install-nightly-task.ps1` (system-state change, prescribed), then Export-ScheduledTask into ops/scheduled-tasks/tc-graph-nightly-matching.xml with the SID replaced by __CURRENT_USER_SID__ and the UTF-16 declaration corrected, the same two edits install-grocery-tasks.ps1's header describes. 5) Enable the scheduler's own record: `wevtutil sl Microsoft-Windows-TaskScheduler/Operational /e:true` - REQUIRES ELEVATION (this shell's identity is not in Administrators: IsInRole=False). If the developer cannot elevate, record the step as blocked in this item with the one-line command for Brad; it is diagnostic capability, not a ruling.

items.root_cause: Three layers, each measured. (1) THE MISS: every TC task runs as an InteractiveToken with one occurrence per day and no repetition. A Windows Update restart that lands on the sign-in screen makes every occurrence between the reboot and the next sign-in unrunnable, and StartWhenAvailable does not re-queue an occurrence refused for lack of a session (measured: a session from 03:29, three later Interactive tasks fired, the nightly did not). The 21:30 slot is the most exposed one in the estate because Windows Update's outside-active-hours restart lands in the evening; the morning tasks recover only because Brad signs in before 07:00. A lost night costs the graph a day of matching and pushes every later question one day; a second consecutive miss would have paged as a 61h stale and STILL had no catch-up. (2) THE CLASS THE ALERT BODY NAMES: task registration and task watching are two hand-maintained tables (four registrars; expected-automations.json; ops/scheduled-tasks/*.xml as a third copy), and the only change-time join covers three of the five tasks. A task registered outside that trio is noticed the NEXT MORNING by the heartbeat's TASK UNWATCHED line, which is an alarm whose only follower is a human typing an entry - the graph nightly took three mornings, the harvest crawl was likewise hand-added, and the next registrar will repeat it. (3) THE FALSE GREEN: nightly.ps1 starts its dated run transcript for every verb, so a -StopOnly typed by hand manufactures a log that looks like a run.

root_fix.what: Make a task impossible to register unwatched: every registrar exports its committed definition, the hermetic registry gate covers EVERY committed definition (not the three it owns), and a static detector fails the push when a Register-ScheduledTask call site has no committed definition - so 'registered but unwatched' is a red push gate at change time instead of a morning email
root_fix.exact_change: 1) ops/install-grocery-tasks.ps1: Test-RegistryAgrees is fed the set of task names read from ops/scheduled-tasks/*.xml (the <URI> field, via Get-XmlField) in addition to $OWNED, so a definition committed by any registrar must be named in expected-automations.json or -VerifyRegistry exits 2; items.deviation:
Everything in the item shipped except the elevation step. Five recorded departures, three of them defects found while implementing and fixed in this run.

(1) StopAtDurationEnd IS LEFT FALSE, against the plan's exact_change, and this is the one that matters. It does NOT control whether occurrences fire in daylight - the RepetitionDuration already does that - it controls whether Task Scheduler KILLS a chain still running when the duration ends. A scheduler kill terminates the process and skips the PowerShell finally block that hands the card back, so llama-server would hold 13 GB through the 07:00 and 08:00 sweeps: the exact failure this lane exists to end, and the one install-nightly-task.ps1's own ExecutionTimeLimit comment already forbids ('Task Scheduler killing the process would skip the finally block that hands the card back, so it must only ever fire when the script's own deadline has already failed to'). It would also kill the 05:30 catch-up occurrence at the instant it started, retiring the last chance the plan explicitly wanted to keep. The plan's stated intent - nothing fires in daylight, the card is never held past 06:30 - is fully met with it false. Pinned by a must-fire so it cannot drift back.

(2) BLOCKED, NEEDS ELEVATION: `wevtutil sl Microsoft-Windows-TaskScheduler/Operational /e:true` was attempted and REFUSED. Measured, not assumed: WindowsPrincipal.IsInRole(Administrator) = False for DESKTOP-L652I1V\\Owner, wevtutil exited 5 with 'Failed to save configuration or activate log ... Access is denied.', and Get-WinEvent -ListLog still reads IsEnabled=False afterwards. Nothing else in the item depends on it; it is diagnostic capability, not a ruling. One line for Brad, from an elevated prompt: wevtutil sl Microsoft-Windows-TaskScheduler/Operational /e:true

(3) THE REFUSAL IS A PURE FUNCTION IN EACH REGISTRAR, not inline code. The plan asked both registrars to REFUSE to register an unwatched task; written inline neither refusal could be reached by a self-test, which is the 2026-07-29 same-day-regression shape. It is now Test-TaskWatched, pure over the parsed registry, fixtured in both files, and install-nightly-task.ps1 gained a -SelfTest switch (11 cases) so run-gates discovers it. The two copies are deliberate - the lanes must not depend on each other - and cannot drift apart silently because ops/audit-task-registration.ps1 fails the push on a literal-naming registrar that does not carry the refusal.

(4) THE NEW AUDIT'S LIVE HALF IS HERMETIC AND IS REGISTERED IN run-gates' $static, which is the decision the plan left to the developer. It reads .ps1 source, ops/scheduled-tasks/*.xml and grocery/expected-automations.json, all tracked, so it is green on a bare checkout; run-gates' header rule puts exactly that class in $static and leaves data-dependent audits to the daily chain. Registered rather than left to discovery for the reason audit-write-only-reports records: discovery runs the FIXTURE, the $static entry runs the DETECTOR over the real tree, and only the second can see a registrar somebody adds tomorrow. TWO REAL DEFECTS IN THAT AUDIT WERE FOUND BY RUNNING IT AND FIXED IN THIS RUN, both with frozen fixtures: PowerShell's -match is case-insensitive, so 'Unregister-ScheduledTask' was being read as a registration and both real registrars came back 'could not be resolved' (now a case-sensitive lookbehind anchor); and block comments were not stripped, so ops/audit-run-log-claims.ps1's header sentence describing the rejected 'grep every Register-ScheduledTask' design parsed as a call site - the same block-comment blindness ops/audit-task-registry.ps1's header already records against run-gates' self-test discovery. Same exclusion set as run-gates line 52.

Widening it would make -Verify go BLIND at exit 3 on any box that does not have the other two tasks registered, and the plan's own instruction is to keep $OWNED for the ownership scope.
